module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 226

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/226](https://www.erdosproblems.com/226)
- [BaSc70] Barth, K. F. and Schneider, W. J., *Entire functions mapping
  countable dense subsets of the reals onto each other monotonically*.
  J. London Math. Soc. (2) (1970), 620--626.
- [BaSc71] Barth, K. F. and Schneider, W. J., *Entire functions mapping
  arbitrary countable dense sets and their complements onto each other*.
  J. London Math. Soc. (2) (1971/72), 482--488.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., *Research problems in function theory: new problems*.
  (1974), 155--180.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos226

/-- A real function preserves rationality. -/
def PreservesRationality (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ) ↔ f x ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ)

/--
Is there an entire non-linear function $f$ such that, for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$, $x$ is rational if and only if $f(x)$ is?

Barth and Schneider [BaSc70] proved the stronger result for countable dense subsets of
$\mathbb{R}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos226.lean"]
theorem erdos_226 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ F : ℂ → ℂ, Differentiable ℂ F ∧ (∀ x : ℝ, (F x).im = 0) ∧
      (∀ g : AffineMap ℝ ℝ ℝ, (fun x : ℝ => (F x).re) ≠ g) ∧
      PreservesRationality (fun x : ℝ => (F x).re) := by
  sorry

end Erdos226

reformulations.difference: The source asks for a nonlinear entire function whose values at real inputs are rational exactly when the inputs are rational. Lean explicitly requires real values on the real axis, tests rationality of their real parts, and expresses nonlinearity by excluding all real affine maps from the real restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An entire function mapping rational inputs to rational outputs is continuous, so its imaginary part vanishes on all real inputs by density of the rationals. Consequently, rationality of its real part is exactly rationality of its complex value. For an entire function real-valued on the real axis, its real restriction is affine if and only if the entire function has the form az+b: the nontrivial direction follows from the identity theorem. AffineMap ℝ ℝ ℝ represents exactly the functions x ↦ ax+b. The complete equivalence between the Lean existential and this direct complex-valued formulation was proved as Review226.statement_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; its axioms exclude sorryAx.

review.notes:
Checked both declarations and the checklist's applicable quantifier, domain, answer-polarity, definition, and boundary checks. Lean tests reject every constant function, exclude identity and translations as affine, and show that x² fails rationality preservation at √2. The accessible Erdős Problems snapshot records an affirmative solution and PROVED (LEAN), consistent with research solved and answer(True).

Access limitations: the live problem page was Cloudflare-blocked, so the archived page and Hayman–Lingham's LaTeX supplied the mathematical source evidence. Original publisher article/chapter texts could not be obtained. The cited external proof has an equivalent conclusion and contains no sorry or custom axioms in its source. Its stated toolchain is Lean/Mathlib v4.29.1; replay under the sandbox's v4.33.1 encountered compatibility errors, so I did not independently certify that full proof. This is not evidence of a mathematical or status defect. The repository was left unchanged.
